seo_desc: 13 Christmas events for kids in Seguin, TX for 2026, 4 free: Northern Lights Drive-Thru Christmas Lights on Church Road and Santa's Workshop and Live Reindeer.
lede: Seguin opens the season with its Holiday Stroll weekend downtown, then spreads Christmas out to a lit-up heritage farm on Cordova Road, a drive-through light show on Church Road and carols at Texas Lutheran University.
celebrates: The first weekend of December belongs to the Holiday Stroll. A lighted parade of more than 100 entries rolls south on Austin Street to Central Park, where the mayor switches on the downtown lights and Santa poses for photos. The next evening is Sip n' Stroll, when downtown shops pour more than a dozen homemade hot chocolates, and on Saturday nonprofits run the North Pole Stroll for children in Central Park. The Seguin Art League's Yulefest closes the weekend at the Seguin Coliseum. Around it, A Stroll to the Stable fills the Nolte Building with nativity sets, Texas Lutheran University holds Christmas Vespers, and the Big Red Barn hosts Country Christmas.
lastyear: In 2025 the Holiday Stroll Parade stepped off on Thursday, December 4, at 6:30 pm, with more than 70 floats heading down Austin Street from College Street to Central Park and Santa and Mrs. Claus at the end. Mayor Donna Dodgen then switched on the downtown lights while families lined up for food trucks and photos with Santa. That year also brought a brand-new tradition, A Stroll to the Stable, with nativity displays and music in the historic Nolte Building from December 4 to 7, and the North Pole Stroll added a shoebox parade.
facts: Seguin's railroad tracks sit about a mile from the Guadalupe County Courthouse because of John Ireland, the Seguin lawmaker nicknamed the Sage of Seguin who later became governor. He pushed through a rule that a railroad passing a county town could not put its depot more than a mile from the courthouse. To make that mile easier on muddy North Austin Street, a mule-drawn streetcar started running in 1886, and it kept going until the street was paved around 1915.
trains: The Galveston, Harrisburg and San Antonio Railroad reached Seguin in late 1875 and became part of the Southern Pacific, and the town still sits on that main line. Amtrak's Sunset Limited rolls through, but trains have not stopped in Seguin since Amtrak took over in 1971. The nearest Amtrak stations are San Antonio, served by the Sunset Limited and Texas Eagle, and San Marcos on the Texas Eagle. For a train day, try the Texas Transportation Museum in San Antonio, the San Antonio Railroad Heritage Museum in Elmendorf, or the Austin Steam Train Association's North Pole Flyer.

Country Christmas at the Big Red Barn
Santa in the Pecan Museum, hayrides through the lights and carols in the old Zion Church on a farm worked since the 1850s.
Texas Lutheran University's choirs lead a service of music in Jackson Auditorium, and the audience sings carols with them.
kidfact: Long ago, a mule pulled a little streetcar up and down North Austin Street to carry people from the train station to the courthouse, and stories from the time call the mule Maud.
faq: When is the Seguin Holiday Stroll?

The Holiday Stroll takes place on the first weekend of December. It opens on Thursday evening with the lighted Holiday Stroll Parade on Austin Street, followed by Sip n' Stroll on Friday, the Jingle Bell Run and North Pole Stroll on Saturday, and Yulefest at the Seguin Coliseum on Sunday. A Stroll to the Stable runs in the Nolte Building around the same days.
Where does the Seguin Christmas parade go?

The Holiday Stroll Parade starts at the intersection of Austin Street and College Street and travels south on Austin Street to Central Park. When it ends, the mayor switches on the downtown holiday lights and Santa is in the park for photos, so Central Park is the place to finish the night.
Where can kids see Santa in Seguin?

Santa appears at the end of the Holiday Stroll Parade in Central Park and at the North Pole Stroll, where nonprofits offer pictures with Santa. At Country Christmas, Santa sits in the Pecan Museum at the Big Red Barn on Cordova Road, and the Northern Lights drive-through on Church Road has a live Santa at its photo stop.
What is the World's Largest Pecan?

It is a giant pecan displayed under a pavilion at the Texas Agricultural Education and Heritage Center, known as the Big Red Barn, home of the Pecan Museum of Texas. During Country Christmas the pecan is dressed in Christmas lights along with the farm's Heritage Village.

highlights: Country Christmas at the Big Red Barn on December 11 and 12 puts Santa in the Pecan Museum, home of the World's Largest Pecan, with hayrides through a lit Heritage Village; a family ticket is $25.
Northern Lights on Church Road is a one-mile drive-through light show open nightly from 6 to 10 pm, November 27 through January 2, at $28.96 per car online.
A Stroll to the Stable shows more than 500 nativity sets free in the historic Nolte Building downtown, November 27 to December 6.
Seguin Public Library's Polar Express Interactive Movie is Saturday, December 12, 2 to 4 pm; registration is required and opens November 27 at 9 am, per the library calendar.
Sip n' Stroll on Friday, December 4, 6 to 9 pm, has over a dozen homemade hot chocolates, live entertainment and photos with Santa in downtown Seguin, per Visit Seguin.
